text:
Evidence supports scale normalization before additive fusion, but I found no direct validation of this exact SASRec–history-cosine margin-ratio rule. [Retrieval fusion research](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0169023X11001236) motivates making component scores comparable. Algebraically, for paired margins Δs=s⁺−s⁻ and Δc=c⁺−c⁻, scoring s+λkc with k=SD(Δs)/SD(Δc) equalizes their margin standard deviations before λ. This is a scale heuristic, not probability calibration or an optimal ranking weight: it ignores mean margins and correctness. Correlation also matters: Var(Δs+λkΔc)=σs²(1+λ²+2λρ). Shared embeddings can make the signals redundant; equal scales do not establish complementary information.

Standard deviation captures tail variation but is outlier-sensitive; normalized MAD (1.4826×MAD) or IQR/1.349 provide robust alternatives, although they can suppress ranking-relevant tails and become zero with ties. [NIST](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda356.htm) supports robust scales for long-tailed distributions. Recommended safeguards, rather than established guarantees: estimate category-specific scales on fixed, causal training-prefix pairs with the frozen model in evaluation mode; exclude padding and nonfinite values; impose a meaningful denominator floor, cap k, and disable the residual when its scale is negligible. Save scales, sampling seeds, estimator settings and λ with the predictor.

Transfer remains empirical. Training-prefix positives and sampled negatives need not represent held-out next-item margins; full-catalog top ranks emphasize extreme competitors. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse full-ranking model comparisons. Select λ, including zero, using the pinned macro validation HR@10; compare robust-scale variants within budget. Gains against 99 negatives do not establish gains for full-catalog recommendations.
